historical_reviews.history: Round-2 retained this exact row UNRESOLVED. The approved row-1800 BMC-board Final Audit decision establishes that an absent board I2C specification containing the entire operation contract remains BLOCKED, while its BMC identity/evidence do not transfer to this MB case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The project I2C ownership rule defaults this scope to BMC/platform management and requires controller, bus, address, access path, vendor specification and expected output.

original_test_intent: Validate the motherboard I2C topology and device responses defined by a platform specification, without guessing which controller, bus, mux path, address or probe operation belongs to MB coverage.
original_method: The source delegates procedure and criteria entirely to an absent specification. No I2C enumeration, scan, read, force or write command is authorized until that specification is attached and this row is freshly reviewed.
manual_activity: Platform/I2C owners must attach the motherboard-specific controller/bus/mux/address/ownership specification and acceptance matrix before any probe can be designed.
required_inputs: Approved motherboard I2C specification and platform revision
safety_requirements: Do not run generic i2cdetect against every visible bus
Do not assume host /dev/i2c nodes reach the MB requirement
Do not use force, quick-write or write-capable transactions
Do not expose credentials or disable host verification
Preserve BMC, sensor, PMBus and OS evidence
Stop on management, telemetry, bus or device anomaly
agent_execution_scope: Do not borrow BMC-board or switch-board maps
Request fresh review after inputs exist
engineer_actions: Define the motherboard I2C controller and ownership
Approve bus/mux/address/device matrix and safe transaction

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The loop scans every host-visible bus with generic i2cdetect probes, although the source names no motherboard bus, address, device or safe transaction. It can touch unrelated BMC, PMBus, EEPROM and sensor paths and truncates the evidence it claims to return.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: BLOCKED: attach the motherboard I2C specification and define a controller/bus/mux/address allowlist before a bounded command is designed.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The I2C MB identity and two-minute attended/machine estimates are preserved; no unprovided operation is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After the spec is approved, use the documented BMC/OOB path and only its permitted transaction on the exact MB bus/mux/address set, comparing complete raw responses with the expected device matrix and correlating platform health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Converts the placeholder reference into a specification-bound, allowlisted transaction rather than a host-wide scan.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Host bus enumeration alone cannot demonstrate access to the intended motherboard management segment or validate expected devices and responses.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some address probes issue real bus transactions that can disturb EEPROM, sensor, PMBus or controller state; ownership and safe operation must precede tool selection.

project_override_considerations: Apply the Wistron rule that I2C is BMC/platform-management scope by default; require the MB controller/bus/mux/address, BMC/OOB path, vendor specification and expected output before execution.
expected_evidence: Approved MB I2C specification and fresh review
Exact bus/mux/address/device allowlist and permitted transaction
Complete untruncated raw responses with timestamps and exit status
Baseline/post BMC session, sensor, PMBus, SEL/SDR and OS health
Owner disposition for every expected, absent or unexpected device

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source is not internally contradictory; it is incomplete because both procedure and criteria refer to a specification that is not supplied.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The absent MB I2C specification contains the target, operation and acceptance semantics. Package installation or user confirmation cannot safely invent those facts, and generic probing may affect platform-management devices.

engineering_decision_request.question: Define Functionality row 1799 Wistron-HW-00001-V003 I2C MB: approved platform/board revision, BMC or OOB controller and access path, bus/mux/address/device map, reserved exclusions, permitted transaction, expected responses, acceptance, health monitoring and recovery; preserve the Master placeholders and require fresh review before any bus access.

review_improvement: Changes the optimistic package-gated treatment to BLOCKED because the missing referenced specification is the whole motherboard I2C test contract, not an operator parameter.
independent_technical_reasoning: An I2C bus number has meaning only within a controller and mux topology. A generic host scan cannot distinguish the intended motherboard segment from BMC, PMBus, EEPROM or sensor paths, and even nominal discovery probes can alter device behavior. Without the referenced map and expected response, neither safe execution nor PASS is definable.
